subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, Hᵏ := μHE[k], L¹ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ, Φ(s, x) := (s, x_1, …, x_P) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))), Φ′(p) := Φ(p.1, p.2) for p ∈ ℝ × ℝ^P, π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))) and y₀ := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y) 0. Assume (MP): for every A ⊆ ℝ^P that is Hᵐ-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and has Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A). Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Hᵐ-null-measurable and countably m-rectifiable with Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P. Then the restriction of H^{m+1} to the slab S_A := {y ∈ ℝ^{P+1} : π(y) ∈ A ∧ y₀ ∈ (0, 1)} is the push-forward under Φ′ of (L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ (Hᵐ⌞A): H^{m+1}⌞S_A = Φ′_*((L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A).

Source: derived fact (D2) (product sets) of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary admissible A (after the split the parent uses it through the sibling slab_transfer, with A = M and A = M ∩ π(K′)).

Notation (as in the parent). E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1), Hᵏ := μHE[k], L¹ := Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ, equiv_n := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) ℝ : Eucl n ≃L[ℝ] (Fin n → ℝ). Φ(s, x) := equiv_{P+1}⁻¹(Fin.cons s (equiv_P x)) = (s, x_1, …, x_P); Φ′ : ℝ × E → E′, Φ′(p) := Φ(p.1, p.2); π(y) := equiv_P⁻¹(Fin.tail (equiv_{P+1} y)) = (y_1, …, y_P); y₀ := equiv_{P+1}(y)(0); O := {y ∈ E′ : y₀ ∈ (0,1)}; for A ⊆ E, S_A := {y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ A ∧ y₀ ∈ (0,1)} and ν_A := Hᵐ⌞A. Coordinate facts (Fin.cons/Fin.tail computations with ContinuousLinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, symm_apply_apply, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ, Fin.tail_cons, Fin.cons_self_tail): (F1) π(Φ(s,x)) = x, (Φ(s,x))₀ = s and Φ(y₀, π(y)) = y. (MP) is the hypothesis: for every A ⊆ E that is Hᵐ-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and has Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, H^{m+1}⌞{y : π(y) ∈ A} = Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ Hᵐ⌞A).

1. (ν_A is s-finite.) Let K ⊆ E be compact. K is closed, hence Borel, so ν_A(K) = Hᵐ(K ∩ A) = Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ (Measure.restrict_apply, inter_comm, hypothesis on A). Thus ν_A is finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts). Since E is σ-compact, ν_A is σ-finite, in particular s-finite (instance inference from IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts); this is the instance used by Measure.prod_restrict in Step 6.
2. (Φ′ is Borel.) p ↦ Fin.cons p.1 (equiv_P p.2) is continuous (Continuous.finCons with continuous_fst and equiv_P ∘ snd), and equiv_{P+1}⁻¹ is continuous, so Φ′ is continuous, hence measurable.
3. (O is Borel.) y ↦ y₀ = equiv_{P+1}(y)(0) is continuous (continuous_apply 0 composed with equiv_{P+1}) and (0,1) is a Borel set, so O is Borel (measurableSet_Ioo.preimage).
4. (Preimage of O.) For p = (s, x), (Φ′(p))₀ = equiv_{P+1}(equiv_{P+1}⁻¹(Fin.cons s (equiv_P x)))(0) = (Fin.cons s (equiv_P x))(0) = s (apply_symm_apply, Fin.cons_zero). Hence Φ′⁻¹(O) = (0,1) × E (= Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ univ).
5. (Set identity.) y ∈ S_A ⟺ (π(y) ∈ A ∧ y₀ ∈ (0,1)) ⟺ (y₀ ∈ (0,1) ∧ π(y) ∈ A), so S_A = O ∩ {y : π(y) ∈ A}.
6. (Computation.) H^{m+1}⌞S_A = H^{m+1}⌞(O ∩ {π ∈ A}) (Step 5) = (H^{m+1}⌞{π ∈ A})⌞O (Measure.restrict_restrict, O Borel by Step 3) = (Φ′_*(L¹ ⊗ ν_A))⌞O ((MP) applied to A, whose three hypotheses are exactly the assumptions on A) = Φ′_*((L¹ ⊗ ν_A)⌞Φ′⁻¹(O)) (Measure.restrict_map: Φ′ measurable by Step 2, O Borel) = Φ′_*((L¹ ⊗ ν_A)⌞((0,1) × E)) (Step 4) = Φ′_*((L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ (ν_A⌞E)) (Measure.prod_restrict, using Step 1) = Φ′_*((L¹⌞(0,1)) ⊗ ν_A) (Measure.restrict_univ). ∎

2. (Finiteness.) For compact K, ν_A(K) = Hᵐ(K ∩ A) = Hᵐ(A ∩ K) < ∞ (Measure.restrict_apply, K Borel), so ν_A is finite on compact sets, hence σ-finite and s-finite (instance inference from IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts, E σ-compact). Φ′ is a homeomorphism ℝ × E → E′ with inverse y ↦ (y₀, π(y)): (y₀, π(y)) at y = Φ′(s, x) equals (s, x) by (F1), and Φ′(y₀, π(y)) = equiv_{P+1}⁻¹(Fin.cons (equiv_{P+1} y 0) (Fin.tail (equiv_{P+1} y))) = y (Fin.cons_self_tail); Φ′ is continuous (Continuous.finCons) and the inverse is continuous (Continuous.prodMk of the coordinate map y ↦ y₀ and of π, the latter by continuous_pi over the coordinates i.succ). 4. (Composition with π.) For p = (s, x), π(Φ′(p)) = equiv_P⁻¹(Fin.tail (Fin.cons s (equiv_P x))) = equiv_P⁻¹(equiv_P x) = x (apply_symm_apply, Fin.tail_cons, symm_apply_apply). Hence (h ∘ π) ∘ Φ′ = h ∘ Prod.snd pointwise, for every function h on E.
5. (Proof of (a).) Let f be Hᵐ-integrable on A, i.e. f is ν_A-integrable. By definition IntegrableOn (f ∘ π) S_A H^{m+1} means that f ∘ π is integrable for H^{m+1}⌞S_A, which is Φ′_*ρ_A by Step 1; by MeasurableEmbedding.integrable_map_iff (Step 3) this is equivalent to ρ_A-integrability of (f ∘ π) ∘ Φ′. Now f ∘ Prod.snd is ρ_A-integrable by Integrable.comp_snd (f ν_A-integrable, L¹⌞(0,1) finite, ν_A s-finite; by Tonelli ∫|f(x)| dρ_A(s, x) = L¹((0,1))·∫|f| dν_A < ∞), and (f ∘ π) ∘ Φ′ = f ∘ Prod.snd pointwise by Step 4 (Integrable.congr). This proves (a).
6. (Proof of (b).) Let g be ν_A-a.e. strongly measurable. By Step 1 and MeasurableEmbedding.aestronglyMeasurable_map_iff (Step 3), g ∘ π is a.e. strongly measurable for H^{m+1}⌞S_A = Φ′_*ρ_A iff (g ∘ π) ∘ Φ′ is a.e. strongly measurable for ρ_A. Prod.snd : ℝ × E → E is measurable and quasi-measure-preserving from ρ_A to ν_A (Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_snd, ν_A s-finite: for Borel B, (Prod.snd)_*ρ_A(B) = ρ_A(ℝ × B) ≤ (L¹⌞(0,1))(ℝ)·ν_A(B) = ν_A(B) (Measure.map_apply, Measure.prod_prod_le), so ν_A(B) = 0 implies (Prod.snd)_*ρ_A(B) = 0), so g ∘ Prod.snd is ρ_A-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_quasiMeasurePreserving). Source: Step 5 of the parent proof (null-measurability of {π ∈ M}); the null-set transfer (D1) that the parent derives from (MP) is taken here as the hypothesis (NT).

Notation. E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1), Hᵏ := μHE[k], equiv_n := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) ℝ : Eucl n ≃L[ℝ] (Fin n → ℝ); π(y) := equiv_P⁻¹(Fin.tail (equiv_{P+1} y)) = (y_1, …, y_P) for y ∈ E′. (NT) is the hypothesis: for every N ⊆ E with Hᵐ(N) = 0, H^{m+1}({y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ N}) = 0 (the null-set transfer (D1) of the parent proof).

1. (π is Borel.) π = equiv_P⁻¹ ∘ (f ↦ Fin.tail f) ∘ equiv_{P+1}; every coordinate y ↦ equiv_{P+1}(y)(i.succ) is continuous (continuous_apply), so π is continuous (continuous_pi, continuity of equiv_P⁻¹) and therefore measurable.

Then (π_*H^{m+1})(B) = H^{m+1}(π⁻¹(B)) (Measure.map_apply, π measurable, B Borel) = H^{m+1}({y : π(y) ∈ B}) = 0 by (NT). Hence π_*H^{m+1} ≪ Hᵐ (Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.mk), and with Step 1, π is quasi-measure-preserving (Measure.QuasiMeasurePreserving π H^{m+1} Hᵐ).
3. (Conclusion.) Since M is Hᵐ-null-measurable there is a Borel set M_B with M =ᵐ[Hᵐ] M_B. Because π is quasi-measure-preserving, π⁻¹(M) =ᵐ[H^{m+1}] π⁻¹(M_B) (QuasiMeasurePreserving.preimage_ae_eq: the set where the indicators of π⁻¹(M) and π⁻¹(M_B) differ is π⁻¹ of the Hᵐ-null set where those of M and M_B differ), and π⁻¹(M_B) is Borel by Step 1. Hence π⁻¹(M) = {y : π(y) ∈ M} is H^{m+1}-null-measurable; this is exactly MeasureTheory.NullMeasurableSet.preimage applied to the quasi-measure-preserving map of Step 2. ∎

(NT) is the hypothesis: for every N ⊆ E with Hᵐ(N) = 0, H^{m+1}({y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ N}) = 0 (the null-set transfer (D1) of the parent proof).

1. (Unpacking.) By CountablyRectifiable m M there are M₀ ⊆ E with Hᵐ(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : Eucl m → E (j ∈ ℕ), F_j K_j-Lipschitz for some K_j ∈ ℝ≥0, with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j.
2. (Three linear maps.) Let hd : Eucl (m+1) → ℝ, hd(u) := u₀ = equiv_{m+1}(u)(0) (the coordinate projection 0 composed with equiv_{m+1}); tl : Eucl (m+1) → Eucl m, tl(u) := equiv_m⁻¹(i ↦ equiv_{m+1}(u)(i.succ)) = (u_1, …, u_m) (ContinuousLinearMap.pi of the projections i.succ, composed with equiv_{m+1} and equiv_m⁻¹); Ψ : ℝ × E → E′, Ψ(a, x) := Φ(a, x). Ψ is additive and homogeneous (apply equiv_{P+1}, which is injective, and compare coordinates with Fin.cases: coordinate 0 is a, coordinate k.succ is x_k), and ℝ × E is finite dimensional, so Ψ is a continuous linear map (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap). Every continuous linear map L is ‖L‖₊-Lipschitz (ContinuousLinearMap.lipschitzWith). (Explicitly |u₀| ≤ ‖u‖, ‖tl u‖ ≤ ‖u‖ and ‖Ψ(a, x)‖ = (a² + ‖x‖²)^{1/2} ≤ √2·max(|a|, ‖x‖), but only Lipschitz continuity is used.)
3. (The Lipschitz parametrizations.) Define G_j(u) := Ψ(hd(u), F_j(tl(u))) = Φ(u₀, F_j(u_1, …, u_m)). The map u ↦ F_j(tl(u)) is K_j‖tl‖₊-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp); the pairing u ↦ (hd(u), F_j(tl(u))) ∈ ℝ × E is max(‖hd‖₊, K_j‖tl‖₊)-Lipschitz for the product (max) distance (LipschitzWith.prodMk); hence G_j is ‖Ψ‖₊·max(‖hd‖₊, K_j‖tl‖₊)-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp). In particular ∃ K, LipschitzWith K G_j for every j.
4. (The exceptional set.) Put C₀ := {y ∈ E′ : π(y) ∈ M₀} (a full cylinder, not intersected with any slab). By (NT), H^{m+1}(C₀) = 0.

Put u := equiv_{m+1}⁻¹(Fin.cons y₀ (equiv_m w)) ∈ Eucl (m+1). subproblems.title: The extended frame (e₀, ιτ_1, …, ιτ_m) is orthonormal
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, e₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{P+1} and ι(v) := (0, v_1, …, v_P) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} for v ∈ ℝ^P (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ v))). If τ = (τ_1, …, τ_m) is an orthonormal family in ℝ^P, then τ̃ := (e₀, ιτ_1, …, ιτ_m) (Lean: Fin.cons e₀ (fun i => ι (τ i)) : Fin (m+1) → ℝ^{P+1}) is an orthonormal family in ℝ^{P+1}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (τ : Fin m → Eucl P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → Orthonormal ℝ (Fin.cons (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 : Eucl (P + 1)) (fun i => (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ (τ i)))) : Fin (m + 1) → Eucl (P + 1))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 10(c)(i) of the parent proof (orthonormality of τ̃), using the inner-product formula (F3).

Notation. equiv_n := EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) ℝ; Φ(a, u) := equiv_{P+1}⁻¹(Fin.cons a (equiv_P u)) for a ∈ ℝ, u ∈ ℝ^P, so ι(v) = Φ(0, v); ⟨·,·⟩ is the Euclidean inner product.

1. (F3) For a, b ∈ ℝ and u, w ∈ ℝ^P, ⟨Φ(a,u), Φ(b,w)⟩ = ab + ⟨u, w⟩. Indeed the inner product of EuclideanSpace is the sum over coordinates, ⟨x, z⟩ = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (P+1)} x_i z_i (PiLp.inner_apply; for reals ⟨r, t⟩ = t·r). Split the sum with Fin.sum_univ_succ: the i = 0 term is a·b (coordinate 0 of Φ(a,u) is a by Fin.cons_zero) and the i = k.succ terms are u_k w_k (Fin.cons_succ), whose sum is ⟨u, w⟩ (PiLp.inner_apply again; commutativity of multiplication).
2. (e₀ in coordinates.) e₀ = Φ(1, 0): apply the injective map equiv_{P+1} and compare coordinates (Fin.cases): coordinate 0 of e₀ is 1 and coordinate k.succ is 0, and the same holds for Fin.cons 1 (equiv_P 0).
3. (Orthonormality criterion.) By orthonormal_iff_ite, τ̃ is orthonormal iff ⟨τ̃_i, τ̃_j⟩ = (if i = j then 1 else 0) for all i, j ∈ Fin (m+1), and the hypothesis gives ⟨τ_k, τ_l⟩ = (if k = l then 1 else 0) for k, l ∈ Fin m. Note τ̃_0 = e₀ = Φ(1, 0) (Fin.cons_zero, Step 2) and τ̃_{k.succ} = Φ(0, τ_k) (Fin.cons_succ).
4. (Case analysis by Fin.cases on i and j.) (i = j = 0) ⟨Φ(1,0), Φ(1,0)⟩ = 1·1 + ⟨0,0⟩ = 1. (i = 0, j = l.succ) ⟨Φ(1,0), Φ(0,τ_l)⟩ = 1·0 + ⟨0, τ_l⟩ = 0, and 0 ≠ l.succ (Fin.succ_ne_zero), so the right side is 0. (i = k.succ, j = 0) ⟨Φ(0,τ_k), Φ(1,0)⟩ = 0·1 + ⟨τ_k, 0⟩ = 0, and k.succ ≠ 0. (i = k.succ, j = l.succ) ⟨Φ(0,τ_k), Φ(0,τ_l)⟩ = 0·0 + ⟨τ_k, τ_l⟩ = (if k = l then 1 else 0) = (if k.succ = l.succ then 1 else 0) (Fin.succ_inj). Hence τ̃ is orthonormal. ∎
